text:
Kavi: FYI Legal just asked for deletion proof for a DSAR covering embeddings + snaps. Our nightly KMS rotation overlaps the SLA window. Ideas?
Riley: We should emit an immediate tombstone in Audit S3 (append-only) and mark deletion_state=pending_signed. Then later attach the KMS signature referencing the tombstone version. That lets us meet DSAR timeline.
Anya: Agreed. Also need a narrow RBAC role privacy-erasure with s3:DeleteObject scoped to embeddings prefix + snapshots:DeleteSnapshot for specific snapshot ARNs. Two-person approval for cross-region deletes.
Sarah (Legal): Tombstone + follow-up signature is acceptable if we notify the user with expected timeframe. For vendor WORM backups, Legal needs a retention-exception record with approver and expiry date.
ops-bot: :warning: KMS rotation for keys/erasure-sign at 3130002300-3130002350. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-rotation
Riley: Implementation notes: tombstone payload = single-line JSON (no PII) {request_id, objects[], hashes[], created_ts, created_by, deletion_state}. Upload with object-lock+versioning. Sign canonical(tombstone_version||"|"||request_id) with asymmetric KMS when available. Store .sig next to tombstone.
Anya: Tests: simulate rotation window, ensure pending tombstone sent to user, and ensure signature attached post-rotation. Add alert if tombstone.pending > 48h.
Kavi: I'll open tickets for tombstone writer, IAM role, and runbook updates. Keeping thread as single source of truth. :thumbsup:
